Liz (Support): FYI customer AcmeHealth just escalated — p95 for generation endpoints jumped from ~120ms to 850ms, p99s near 2.6s. Started ~08:42 UTC after the 08:30 deploy. They're hitting production heavily :frowning:
Alex R (Runtime): Thanks Liz. Can you paste traces and a sample request ID? Also any correlation with model variant or region?
Liz (Support): trace id 8f3a2b7c, route /v1/generate, model:redwood-7b-q4. Region us-east-1. Customer says it started immediately after that deploy.
Maya P (SRE): Looking at metrics now. PromQL I ran: 
```
sum by(route) (rate(redwood_inference_latency_seconds_bucket{job="runtime",le="0.5"}[5m]))
```
but more useful: prefix cache hit ratio dropped hard. Query: 
```
avg_over_time(redwood_cache_prefix_hit_ratio{env="prod"}[10m])
```
was ~0.98 before 08:30, now ~0.40. KV cache miss rate spiked correspondingly.
Samir K (Infra): That smells like cache key fragmentation / thrash. Any recent changes to key generation or request-id propagation in the runtime?
Alex R (Runtime): We shipped a small change to prefix cache key construction in that deploy: added request.headers["x-client-id"] to the cache key to respect tenant scoping. It was meant to be optional but I see a PR flag that made it always included. If clients send ephemeral header values we could be creating near-unique keys.
Jo (ML Eng): That would definitely kill hit rate. If every request includes a per-request nonce in headers, adding it to the key = no reuse.
Jules (Oncall SRE): Repro steps: I replayed a few requests with the same prompt but different request-ids and saw cache keys differ. Example: 
```
# generated key excerpts from runtime logs
prefix_key="pref::model:redwood-7b::prompt_hash:af3e::client:acme"
prefix_key="pref::model:redwood-7b::prompt_hash:af3e::client:acme::xid:aa2f9"
prefix_key="pref::model:redwood-7b::prompt_hash:af3e::client:acme::xid:bb7d"
```
so the xid/request-id got appended. Cache eviction skyrockets because working set exploded.
Alex R (Runtime): Confirmed. The offending commit is 7a9d2b — I pushed a fix to stop including ephemeral header values and instead use a stable tenant id header (x-tenant-id) when present. I can cut a hotfix.
Maya P (SRE): Immediate mitigations: 1) roll the runtime deploy back to previous stable (we have a rollback window), OR 2) apply hotfix build to gate (canary) and prod if tests pass. While we decide, we can also increase prefix cache capacity and temporarily change eviction policy to reduce thrash.
Samir K (Infra): Increasing capacity is quick but might be wasteful if keys are really unique. I can bump the prefix cache pool by 2x in prod for a short window. That should reduce p99 while we patch.
Liz (Support): AcmeHealth wants ETA. Can we get an interim rollback or hotfix ETA?
Alex R (Runtime): Hotfix build passes unit tests. I'll deploy to canary in 5m. If canary shows prefix hit ratio recovery and p95 drop, we'll promote. If not, I'll roll back. ETA ~20-30m.
DeployBot: Canary deploy started: runtime-service/7a9d2b-hotfix -> canary (replicas=2).
Maya P (SRE): Watching metrics: after canary deploy, prefix hit ratio on canary instances jumped back to 0.96 within 2 minutes. Overall prod baseline improved from 0.42 to 0.6 (we're only routing partial traffic to canary). p95 for canary routes ~130ms.
Jules (Oncall SRE): Running quick warmup to prepopulate hot prefixes for Acme tenant: script below (redis-backed prefix cache):
```
# warmup top hot prompts for tenant acme
python tools/prefix_warmup.py --tenant acme --prompts-file top_prompts_acme.txt --target-host redis-prod-1:6379
```
Ran it once, warmed ~1.2k keys. Hit ratio bumped further.
Samir K (Infra): I bumped prefix cache pool from 4GB to 8GB for 15 minutes. Eviction metric dropped by 70%. Note: watch memory. If it climbs >85% we'll revert.
Liz (Support): I'll tell customer we're rolling a hotfix and warming their hot prefixes, ETA ~30m, monitoring closely.
Alex R (Runtime): After successful canary I'm promoting hotfix to prod. DeployBot: runtime-service/7a9d2b-hotfix -> prod (replicas=24) started.
Maya P (SRE): Post-prod-deploy numbers: prefix hit ratio now ~0.93 across prod, KV miss rate back to baseline, p95 returned to ~140ms, p99 under 400ms. Solid.
Jo (ML Eng): Long term we should: 1) add linter/test to prevent ephemeral headers in cache key composition, 2) emit metric of "cache_key_entropy" or cardinality estimate to detect runaway uniqueness, 3) change eviction from plain LRU to segmented-LRU (W-TinyLFU) for better hotspot retention.
Alex R (Runtime): Agreed. Also adding a guard in code: only include header values in keys if flag immutable_header=True at config time, and add per-tenant allowlist for header-based scoping. I'll open RFC + follow-up PRs.
Maya P (SRE): I'll create an alert: fire when prefix_hit_ratio < 0.7 for >3m and eviction_rate > x. Also add synthetic replay tests in staging that assert hit ratio > 0.8 for common workloads.
Jules (Oncall SRE): Notes for postmortem: root cause = unintended inclusion of ephemeral request header in prefix cache key. Contributing factors: lack of guard/lint, no cardinality monitoring, no canary traffic split for this path (deploy shipped to most prod hosts).
Liz (Support): Customer updated: thanks, they see response times back to normal and are happy with the quick fix.
Alex R (Runtime): I'll draft a short changelog and add the follow-up tasks. Thanks everyone for the quick triage. :thumbsup:
DeployBot: Prod deploy successful.
Jules (Oncall SRE): Closing loop — will assign postmortem and remediate followups. If anyone wants to add notes for the postmortem thread, drop them here.
